title: Mine
author: Robert McCammon
review: 3.5/5 I do have some plot criticisms. The prose was great as per usual for RMC. Fairly standard thriller but some interesting elements and the character of Mary was absolutely unhinged but wish we had a bit more depth overall in some of the characters. Glad I read this overall.

The baby woke up with a start, his blue eyes searching and his mouth working the pacifier. He saw strange shapes and unknown colors, and he heard the shrill and bump of muffled sounds: the threshold of a mysterious, frightening world. In a few minutes his heavy eyelids closed. He drifted off to sleep again, innocent of sin, and his hands clutched for a mother who was not there.
Routines were the vital fabric of the Mindfuck State; when a routine was disrupted, like a missed stitch, all the little ants got stirred up. It was time to get out.
Far to go. Far to go. Into the golden West, dark as a tomb.
